head: 0ecee0a9b0713a495a904de5a22fa013bec32ad1
summary: SL-033 committed the startup-hook driver (tests/window/FsaWindowHook, modes stop/throw/close, one IsEnabled && IsVisible gate) and WindowCases C-006, C-012 and O-016, so Stopped, exit 70 and closed-early no longer depend on a hook dll in validate's %TEMP%. The build also added tests/window/WindowMutants.ps1 (8 scratch-copy mutants), which the design had said not to commit. It ran at a low tier with no critique or critique-review, and took 3 builds, 4 code-reviews, 4 validates and 2 spike rows. One lap fixed a real defect (the hook swallowed faults from the handler it pressed); the other changed no code.

payload.summary: SL-033 committed the startup-hook driver (tests/window/FsaWindowHook, modes stop/throw/close, one IsEnabled && IsVisible gate) and WindowCases C-006, C-012 and O-016, so Stopped, exit 70 and closed-early no longer depend on a hook dll in validate's %TEMP%. The build also added tests/window/WindowMutants.ps1 (8 scratch-copy mutants), which the design had said not to commit. It ran at a low tier with no critique or critique-review, and took 3 builds, 4 code-reviews, 4 validates and 2 spike rows. One lap fixed a real defect (the hook swallowed faults from the handler it pressed); the other changed no code.
payload.estimate_error: The tier was one notch low and the size about right for the code. Code volume matched medium: one hook .cs, one class library, Update-Hook, Invoke-HookedRun, 3 cases and a mutant runner. Low risk was wrong for a slice that builds a driver other slices reuse (Pressable and FSA_HOOK_LOG are meant for the tree slice) and injects code into every .NET process that inherits DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS. Low removed critique and critique-review, and both rework laps trace to design-level gaps that layer reviews. Cost ran well past a medium/low slice: 2 spike rows, 3 builds, 4 code-reviews, 4 validates and 15 obligations. Each full validate re-runs about 444 s of window suite (161 s WindowCases All plus 283 s WindowMutants All), so laps are the dominant cost, not code. Size these slices by expected validate laps.

learned.lesson: Risk tier for this project's test-driver slices should follow who reuses the code, not how small the diff is. The low tier skipped critique and critique-review, and the first rework lap and the empty second one both came from design-level gaps. Open the tree slice's hook work at medium so critique runs.
learned.evidence: critique #1 and critique-review #1 recorded 'a low-risk slice... does not get an adversarial review'. Then O-015 (hook swallowed the pressed handler's fault) and O-002 (unfeedable case) cost build #2 and #3, code-review #3 and #4, validate #3 and #4.

learned.lesson: Every case shape the design lists becomes an engine obligation that only a test the engine runs can discharge, so a design that lists 'scratch mutant' shapes cannot also say 'no mutant is committed'. Either commit the runner or mark those cases material:false. The design here decided against committed mutants while listing disabled, collapsed, handler-removed, Exit-rule-removed and compile-error shapes as cases.
learned.evidence: O-003, O-004, O-007, O-009 and O-012 were discharged by tests/window/WindowMutants.ps1 (8 mutants, 283 s), which the design's key_decisions said would not exist. The design's own taste_disagreements called that 'the shape this slice exists to fix'.

learned.lesson: Do not list a timing-race shape as a material case unless the design also names a deterministic feed. 'The scan finishes before the hook acts' cannot be fed deterministically: a small tree opens a scan window of a few ms against the hook's 25 ms poll. Say so in the design, or name the substitute cause. Here O-002 was discharged by StopDisabled, a different cause, and only after a whole extra lap.
learned.evidence: build #3 LEFT OPEN says the 'tree too small' version has no deterministic committed feed. Validate's proof of it stayed in %TEMP%\sl033-validate2\probe-o002.ps1 (10/10 on small and empty trees).

learned.lesson: In this app CancelButton is enabled by XAML default even before a scan. Its Visibility is what tracks a running scan, so the IsVisible half of the hook's Pressable gate is the part that ties a press to a live scan. The tree slice must find the equivalent visible or realised condition for expand and click and cannot assume IsEnabled carries it.
learned.evidence: O-014's discharge: the no-scan step 'showed an enabled but hidden CancelButton'. StopCollapsed made C-006 fail only on 'the hook acted'. C-006 acts at 516-749 ms and stops at about 550 of 30,150 folders.

learned.lesson: Exit 70 has two producers in App.xaml.cs and neither leaves a report: the DispatcherUnhandledException handler (:84-89, Discard plus Shutdown(70)) and the Exit handler that turns exit 0 without a file into 70 (:94-98, d59819e). Tests can tell them apart only by mutant (NoCrashHandler gives 0xE0434352, NoExitRule gives 0). Any new case that asserts 'exit 70, no file' cannot distinguish a fault from an intended close.
learned.evidence: validate #4 not-reached: O-016 cannot tell the Exit rule's 70 from the crash handler's 70. Spike headlines: throw 10/10 exit 70 with no report, close 0/40 reports.

learned.lesson: Any hook mode that presses a control must re-raise a fault from the app's handler onto the dispatcher, and must treat 'refused' after 'acted' as failure. Dispatcher.Invoke from the hook thread rethrows on the hook thread, where Run's catch logs it, so the app's DispatcherUnhandledException never sees it. Use ExceptionDispatchInfo.Capture plus BeginInvoke(Send), as StartupHook.cs:121-133 now does. Expand and click modes must inherit this path.
learned.evidence: code-review #1 m1: with OnCancel mutated to throw, the app finished 30,150/30,150, exited 0 and CheckActed passed on 'acted' then 'refused'. A real click exits 70. Fixed in build #2 (O-015).

learned.lesson: A risk-spike author must read App.xaml.cs's exit and report contract before asserting that a report exists. Two of the three no-gos were the spike's own assumption that exit 70 leaves a report; App.xaml.cs:84-98 already says it does not. They halted the slice and needed a second spike row, and the design had to overrule them.
learned.evidence: design selection_rationale (2): 'the throw no-go and the close no-go were the spikes' own wrong assumption, not app defects'. Measured close 0/40 reports, throw 10/10 exit 70 with no report. Only the disabled/collapsed no-go was a real finding.

learned.lesson: An accepted-pending finding should be built before validate runs. code-review #2 passed with m1 owed, validate #1 then ran a full check and halted 'partial' on O-015, and validate #2 failed it back to build. One full validate was spent to discover a fix the loop already knew was owed.
learned.evidence: run history: code-review #2 pass (1 finding disposed) -> validate #1 halted, O-015 open -> validate #2 fail -> build #2 -> code-review #3 -> validate #3.

learned.lesson: A build that changes no code still costs a full re-verify lap here. build #3 touched nothing in src, tests or eng, but code-review #4 and validate #4 re-ran WindowCases All (161 s) and WindowMutants All (283 s) plus the probe scripts. The validator chose to re-run 'instead of carrying attempt 2's numbers forward'. Budget for that whenever an obligation may land after a pass.
learned.evidence: git diff --stat bd556e5 0ecee0a touched only four .taad/slices/SL-033 records. The same diff limited to src, tests, eng, fitness.yaml, Directory.Build.props, global.json and slnx is empty.

candidates.title: Hook click and expand modes for the tree slice, reusing Pressable and the fault re-raise path
candidates.why: This slice's stated reason was that the tree slice needs click and expand without UIA. Build-check recorded that no expand or click mode was delivered. Pressable was only exercised on CancelButton via FindName, so tree containers (likely virtualised) need their own realised, visible and enabled gate.

candidates.title: Commit the two probes validate only ran from %TEMP%: unknown FSA_HOOK_MODE refused, and relative or ';' hook path refused (criteria 13 and 14)
candidates.why: The design marked both shapes material:false with no separate test, yet validate #4 checked them as criteria 13 and 14 using %TEMP%\sl033-validate2\probe-13-14.ps1. That is the pattern this slice exists to remove, and they would need a hook-mode helper in WindowCases.

candidates.title: A records-only diff must not send code-review and validate through a full re-run
candidates.why: build #3 changed no src, tests or eng file. code-review #4 and validate #4 still re-ran about 444 s of window suite. Staleness should key on code paths (src, tests, eng, fitness.yaml, global.json, slnx), not on the head commit.

candidates.title: Route an accepted-pending finding to build-slice before validate runs
candidates.why: code-review #2 passed with m1/O-015 owed, so validate #1 ran in full and halted partial and validate #2 failed it back to build. The extra validate cost about as much as the fix, which was two edits in StartupHook.cs and CheckActed.

candidates.title: Make O-016 able to tell an intended close from an OnClosing fault
candidates.why: Both the Exit rule and the crash handler give exit 70 with no report, so a future OnClosing fault would still pass O-016. Fixing it needs an app-side signal (for example a distinct exit code) that architecture rule 1 keeps out of a test seam, so it is a product decision.

candidates.title: Let a fresh worktree reuse an SDK 10 instead of downloading 300 MB into its own .dotnet/
candidates.why: This worktree had no .dotnet/ and the machine has only SDK 8.0.425 and 9.0.318 against global.json 10.0.100. build-check declined to run any test, leaving the baseline unknown. The spikes borrowed SL-024\.dotnet. It would amend Q-003's repo-local-only decision.

candidates.title: Reconcile the three drift notes code-review left on StartupHook.cs
candidates.why: code-review #4 says three drift notes from attempt 2 still stand, the first being the comment at StartupHook.cs:127-129 that names OnClosing as reaching the rethrow catch. They are comment-versus-behaviour mismatches in the file the tree slice will extend.

missed.what: The design's hook contract said 'any exception in the hook is caught and logged, never fatal' and ran Act under Dispatcher.Invoke on the hook thread. It never asked what happens when the handler the hook presses (OnCancel via Click, OnClosing via Close) throws. The fault was rethrown on the hook thread and logged 'refused', so the app finished 30,150/30,150 and exited 0 where a real click exits 70. The log contract let CheckActed pass on 'acted' then 'refused'. (Critique did not run: low tier.)
missed.caught_by: code-review #1 as finding m1, reproduced by validate #1, fixed in build #2 (O-015)

missed.what: The design decided 'no mutant build or mutant source is committed, proof lives in validate's record' while listing five scratch-mutant shapes (disabled, collapsed, handler removed, Exit rule removed, compile error or locked dll) as cases owed to build, which only a test the engine runs can discharge. The two could not both hold. (Critique did not run.)
missed.caught_by: build-slice, which committed tests/window/WindowMutants.ps1 to discharge O-003, O-004, O-007, O-009 and O-012, departing from the design

missed.what: The design listed 'the scan finishes before the hook acts' as a material case with no deterministic feed. A small tree's scan window is a few ms against a 25 ms poll, so it can only be proven flakily. The obligation was discharged by a different cause (StopDisabled), and the small-tree proof stayed in validate's %TEMP% probe. (Critique did not run.)
missed.caught_by: the engine, when O-002 landed on build-slice after validate #3 passed (build #3, a no-code lap); build #3 recorded the missing feed as LEFT OPEN

missed.what: The design asserted 'exit 70, no report' for both C-012 (throw) and O-016 (close) without asking what else produces exit 70 with no report. The Exit rule and the crash handler give the same observable, so an OnClosing fault would still pass O-016. Only the NoExitRule mutant shows the 70 comes from the Exit rule on this tree. (Critique did not run.)
missed.caught_by: validate #4, listed as 'not reached: a close-path crash regression'

missed.what: The design judged 'unknown FSA_HOOK_MODE' and 'relative or ;-containing dll path' immaterial with no test. Both came back as acceptance criteria 13 and 14, which validate could prove only with %TEMP% probe scripts. Nothing in the repo would catch a regression in either. (Critique did not run.)

unknowns: Does Pressable transfer to virtualised tree items? Which element carries the enabled and visible gate for expand (the TreeViewItem, its expander ToggleButton, or a container that must first be realised through the ItemContainerGenerator), and does a hook press on it reach the same handler a person's click does? It was only exercised on CancelButton via FindName.

Does a real mouse or UIA press on a CancelButton whose handler throws exit 70 the way the hook's ExceptionDispatchInfo re-raise does? Validate measured the re-raise only, and called the real-click equivalence 'reasoning about WPF, not a measurement'.

Do cases launched under the hook environment stay safe with other managed hosts (dotnet.exe, MSBuild nodes)? Only pwsh 7 was checked. Update-Hook builds before the variables are set, but any future case that shells out to another .NET tool under the hook would be unmeasured.
what_went_wrong: Critique and critique-review were skipped at low tier. Both rework causes (m1's swallowed handler fault and O-002's unfeedable case) plus the mutant-versus-obligation contradiction were design-level gaps, the layer critique reviews. Only code-review, on the diff, found one of them.

The risk-spike halted the slice on 3 no-gos, two of which were the spike's own wrong assumption that exit 70 leaves a report, contradicted by App.xaml.cs:84-98, which build-check had already cited. A halt and a second spike row went on showing the app was right.

code-review #2 passed with m1 accepted-pending. validate #1 then ran a full check and halted 'partial' on O-015, and validate #2 failed it back to build. The fix was two small edits, but it cost an extra full validate before it was built.

O-002 landed on build-slice after validate #3 had passed. build #3 changed no files and discharged it by re-running two existing tests. code-review #4 and validate #4 then re-ran everything (WindowCases All 161 s, WindowMutants All 283 s) on a diff that touched only .taad records. That is one whole lap for a re-attestation.

The design contradicted itself over mutants: it said no committed mutants while listing five mutant-shaped cases the engine can only discharge with a committed test. The builder resolved it by committing WindowMutants.ps1, departing from the design, and nobody had to decide it.

The slice exists to end proof that lives only in validate's %TEMP%, yet it ends with criteria 13 and 14 and O-002's small-tree shape proven only by probe scripts in %TEMP%\sl033-validate2. Validate also left the warm-cache 15-run repeat, Update-Hook against a real leftover exe, and a real input-driven press not run.
